title: 4 GiB is tight; a Keycloak GC burst plus SQL Server's buffer pool can OOM the t3.medium
description: The consolidated stack budgets ~3.95 GiB across 6 services on a 4 GiB host. SQL Server's buffer pool and a Keycloak GC spike can collide. (Category: Operational/Resource; Exposure: High)
mitigation: Per-service memory limits retuned for a 2 vCPU host (the current overlay's cpus:4 is meaningless on t3.medium); 4 GiB swapfile; Keycloak -Xmx384m; drop Seq from UAT. AC-084 asserts no OOM-kill in docker events during an e2e run. Escalate to t3.large if it recurs — upsize, do not split (splitting is 1.8-2x cost and breaks single-host Compose per CON-003).

title: The Keycloak admin console and master-realm token endpoint become internet-facing under /kc/
description: default.conf.template proxies all of /kc/, including /kc/admin and /kc/realms/master. On a real domain this is a password-brute-force surface (was semi-obscure behind ngrok). (Category: Security; Exposure: High)
mitigation: nginx deny on /kc/admin and /kc/realms/master from public; admin access via SSH/SSM tunnel only — consistent with the existing 'admin consoles bind 127.0.0.1' posture (slice P25).
custom_attributes: {"v3_probability": "M", "v3_impact": "H", "disposition_2026_08_17": "MITIGATED BY A CONTROL THIS REPOSITORY NOW OWNS (d968aa3, PR #287) - and it was left OPEN and BLOCKING until that control existed, which is the point of this row. MEASURED FIRST: /kc/admin/, /kc/admin/master/console/ and /kc/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token already answered 404 from the internet, while /kc/realms/acmp/.well-known/openid-configuration correctly answered 200. That looked like a discharge and was NOT accepted as one: deploy/nginx/cloud-443.conf.template had NO admin restriction, so the 404 was Keycloak's own behaviour. A Keycloak upgrade or a hostname change could have turned it into a 200 with nothing in this repository objecting, and nobody would have learned of it until someone went looking. AN ABSENCE OF EXPOSURE YOU DO NOT CONTROL IS NOT A CONTROL. THE FIX: a regex location returning 404 for ^/kc/(admin|realms/master)(/|$) - regex so it wins over `location /kc/` regardless of ordering, and 404 rather than 403 because 403 confirms the path exists and tells a scanner where the admin console lives. PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED: the template was rendered in a throwaway nginx container with a STUB UPSTREAM and probed both ways - the four admin/master paths return 404 and the three SPA paths (OIDC discovery, authorize, KC assets) return 200. The stub is what makes that meaningful: without it every path returns 502, the whole table reads 'blocked', and the test proves nothing. VERIFIED IT BREAKS NOTHING: the ADR-0038 admin client uses KeycloakAdmin__BaseUrl=http://keycloak:8080/ (compose:232, 'the IN-CLUSTER address, not the public one') and kcadm.sh runs inside the container against localhost:8080 - both bypass nginx. COST, recorded so nobody rediscovers it mid-incident: the Keycloak admin console is no longer reachable from a browser; use an SSM port-forward, which is already the admin path since there is no SSH.", "disposed_under": "operator-approved risk review, DEC-050 d2; operator chose to BUILD the control rather than accept the unowned 404"}
